page_title: Things end users care about but programmers don't

sources.entry: Things end users care about but programmers don't: includes colors, formatting, themes, integrations, UX, compatibility, operations.

summary.title: Things end users care about but programmers don't
summary.one_liner: A checklist of end-user expectations (colors, formatting, themes, integrations, UX, compatibility, operations) that developers often underestimate or find hard to implement.
keywords: easy to install update backup software
takeaways: End users often expect fine-grained control over colors, including importing themes, consistent color per item, and automatic contrast.
Formatting expectations include locale-correct numbers and dates, sensible decimal places, and Word-like text editing.
UX expectations cover helpful error messages, undo everywhere, progress indicators, and preventing accidental double actions.
Compatibility and operations items list handling of messy data (malformed CSV/JSON, unknown encodings, ambiguous dates) and easy install, update, backup, and recovery.
summary.summary: This is a bulleted checklist rather than a long-form article. It groups end-user expectations into categories: colors, formatting, themes, integrations, UX, compatibility, and operations. Each category lists specific requests, such as natural sorting, locale-aware date formatting, undo/recover, handling malformed input, and easy backup. The page is a brief opinionated list with no code or implementation details.
